title: How do you answer "What else could the client do?" in a case?
description: Even open questions are structuring questions in disguise. What to do, what to say, and the mistake to avoid.
hook: When the interviewer asks what else the client could do, they want ideas, but they also want order. Here is how to brainstorm in a way that earns marks.
body:
Stage 8 of 10 in the ten stages of a case.

Why it matters

Even open questions are structuring questions in disguise.

The common mistake

Listing ideas randomly, with no priority.

What to do, and what to say

Structure even here

Take a moment and answer as a mini-tree: internal vs external, short vs long term, revenue vs cost. Keep an idea in reserve.

"Let me think about this in two buckets: what we can do with today’s capabilities, and what needs new ones. On the first..."

Add one real example

Tag an idea with real-world experience. It separates good from memorable.

"Retention offers work well here; it’s what mobile operators do when contracts end."

Practise the moment

Read the situation and say your answer out loud before you open the model.

"What could the client do to retain customers?" Open your answer.

Show a strong answer

"Let me think about this in two buckets: things we can do with today’s products and team, and things that need new capabilities. On the first..."

Why it works: Buckets first, then ideas, then a priority.

Add a real-world example to a retention idea.

Show a strong answer

"Retention offers at contract end work well; it’s what mobile operators do just before customers can switch."

Why it works: One real example makes an answer memorable. Use it sparingly.

Next stage: recommendation.
outro: Read it once, then try it on a practice case today while it is fresh. One real attempt teaches more than three re-reads. All ten stages, with every phrase, are on the free perfect casing page.
